harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: node1 now serves HTTPS on TCP/8443 using nginx. A daily persistent timer renews the self-issued 90-day certificate when fewer than 30 days remain and gracefully reloads nginx. The configuration, certificate, firewall rule, and timer all persisted across a verified node reboot.
actions_performed: Installed repository-supported nginx and OpenSSL without changing the RHEL release or kernel.
Restricted the private key to root and configured TLS 1.2/1.3 only.
Enabled nginx, the renewal timer, and the persistent firewalld rule for TCP/8443; no plaintext port 80 listener remains.
Verified automatic threshold renewal with 150 successful concurrent requests and zero failures.
Safely rebooted node1 and verified its changed boot identity and complete service recovery.
Removed temporary test artifacts; retained the original nginx configuration as /etc/nginx/nginx.conf.pre-https-8443 for rollback.

evidence.summary: nginx is active/enabled, listens on IPv4 and IPv6 port 8443, returns the expected HTTPS response, and has persistent runtime firewall access.

evidence.requirement: Automatic certificate renewal before expiration with uninterrupted certificate reload
evidence.summary: The normal renewal service detected a one-day certificate inside its 30-day renewal window, replaced it with a 90-day certificate, changed the serial, and completed 150/150 HTTPS requests without failure during reload.
RHEL 10 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 were retained. Certificate/key matching passed, TLS 1.0 was rejected, TLS 1.3 negotiated successfully, and no units remained failed.

evidence.requirement: node1 mandatory restart persistence and recovery
evidence.summary: Healthy baseline boot ID 180a78a0-8a84-45ff-82f1-cd734208a369 was captured, the safe reboot was acknowledged, and node1 returned with boot ID c53b87e5-fcc8-4c36-81c2-f2aaddda4275. nginx, the timer, certificate serial, HTTPS response, listener, and firewall rule all recovered; the final cleanup audit found no test residue.
